correctness.rationale: In the ordinary alternating CE complex, extending covectors on K by zero on t gives dτ=0 and dη=τ∧(η∘T), where T is multiplication by α; the sign disappears over F₂. The Leibniz rule gives the two-term maps D_r induced additively on the exterior powers. In degree r the dimension is dim ker D_r+dim coker D_(r−1), equal by rank–nullity to the sum of two nullities (including endpoints). Since 1,α,…,α^(d−1) form a basis, T has irreducible separable characteristic polynomial of degree d and eigenvalues α^(2^i). After scalar extension, the exterior derivation has sum, not product, eigenvalues; the r-subsets with sum zero are exactly the weight-r codewords. Frobenius closes the kernel under rotation, and the conjugates are nonzero and distinct, excluding weights one and two. For the converse let R=F₂[X]/(X^d−1) act on K through Frobenius. A normal basis makes K free of rank one as an R-module. For C=(g) choose α as the image of h=(X^d−1)/g; (X^d−1)|ch iff g|c by polynomial cancellation even in repeated-root lengths. Distance ≥3 forces α nonzero of Frobenius orbit length d, since a shorter orbit repeats a conjugate. This includes C=0 using h=1, so all listed profiles occur. The Betti consequences follow by coefficients. The degree-three traces are 0 and 1, so only the first cubic gives the possible weight-three relation; both nonidentity roots in the group of order seven are primitive, and the derived ideal is K, forcing Lie isomorphisms to conjugate the two distinct multiplication polynomials. As a separate even-length check, a root of X^4+X+1 is full-degree and trace zero; a weight-three relation and its one-position shift would yield weight two. Its only nonzero word is 1111 and its Betti polynomial is (1+z)(1+z^4).

arXiv:2610.20153 Theorem 4.4 as comparison for the distinct generalized-cohomology question
value.rationale: The full-degree condition gives a natural irreducible family; its ordinary cohomology initially asks for exterior differential ranks in every degree. The theorem gives an exact independent invariant and the converse answers a realizability question, including the repeated-root case. In particular it separates primitive scalars with different cohomology, explains universal H² vanishing, and detects normality. These are useful structural consequences of the complete classification, not a new name for one computed Betti number or a finite list.
residual_risks: Weight enumerators cannot recover the full code, cup products or the Lie isomorphism class. No counting of nonisomorphic realizations is established.
